title: ZTF visit-deficit deep-fade census: seeded stars at r 16-18.5 whose faint state has no rows, with class tiers, a control-star/injection harness and a Lasair negative-alert live twin
merged_from: R6: Visit-deficit census: ZTF sources whose low state has no rows (expected-visit vs detection count, quadrant-exact)
N1: Below-the-floor fades: a non-detection census of bright ZTF stars (deep dips encoded as detection gaps)
N4: Lane 1 (narrow revival of the closed state-cycler): censored deep-fade census in ZTF DR24, r<=17.5, class-restricted, with Lasair negative-alert live twin
R2: The missing nova-likes: blue non-periodic flickerers at 1-4 kpc (only its 8-year VY Scl low-state census on known nova-likes is kept; the flicker-excess CV screen is parked)
summary: Observable: a contiguous run of expected ZTF quadrant visits (ztf_current_meta_sci polygons + maglimit, filtered to frames released in DR24) with no DR24 row for the target while >=90% of the 10 nearest magnitude-matched controls (same rcid, +/-0.5 mag, <3') have rows: >=8 consecutive frames over >=5 nights (N1) or a >=30-frame / >=3% deficit (R6). Parent: DR24 objects 16.0<r<18.5, ngoodobs>=100, |refmag-medianmag|<0.5, dec>-28, |b|>5-10 (~2e7 objects at |b|>10), plus a bright tier r<=17.5 requiring >=3 mag below the per-frame limit for >=3 yr (N4; Gaia G<17.5, dec>-31 = 135,907,142). Measured pilot facts (R6, one quadrant, 5,769 sources): 97% of the naive deficit tail is quadrant-edge pointing jitter within 5' (63% of visits lost at 3.0', 89% at 4.0'); expected visits are a delta function (median 1044, p90 1046 of 1183 frames); omitting the DR24 epoch cutoff manufactures a spurious 12% deficit; catalogue-level survivors 0/3,000, so the per-source rate is <~1e-5 and the census must run sky-wide (~115k quadrants, ~22,000 deg^2). Kills: edge distance >=5', no brighter Gaia source within 4", no second deficit source within 2', PM<150 mas/yr, shoulder test (last/first row >=1.0 mag fainter than median), per-epoch centroid and mag-vs-limitmag slope, ALeRCE negative alerts as corroboration. Class tiers (N4): (a) M_G<2.5 giants (Gaia17bpp-class long eclipses), (b) blue/GALEX-NUV objects (VY Scl and polar low states), (c) rest (RCB/DY Per declines, UXor dips). Run the same statistic on all VSX nova-likes/polars in the footprint for a VY Scl duty-cycle census (Duffy+2024 did 8 systems; ~1,500-3,000 nova-likes predicted vs ~400 in VSX). Expected: ~1e4 raw flags, 200-400 after the control test, ~100 real deep dippers, 30-80 uncatalogued (N1); bright tier 15-150 raw, 10-40 new (N4); population arithmetic ~300 fully censored state-cyclers at |b|>10 (R6), i.e. 10-50 new-to-knowledge systems. Mandatory before any claim: delete rows from 1,000 random controls over synthetic windows and measure recovery vs gap length; recover the 6 van Roestel+2026 WD obscuration events and 5 AAVSO-documented post-2019 RCB declines at >=9/11; stop and fix if raw survivors exceed ~500. Live twin: nightly Lasair-ZTF filter rmag-srmag1>1.5 AND (ncand-ncandgp)>=10 AND ncandgp_14=0 with the same vetoes, filed to VSX same day. Prioritise gaps after 2020.0 (Gaia DR4 epoch photometry covers only 2014-2020). Window ~12-18 months (Caltech negative-alert machinery; Rubin forced non-detections ~2028). Compute on enzo: column-projected parquet reads of DR24 HATS (~50-100 GB) or ~1,800 per-field TAP pulls (~35 s each); light curves via the HATS object-ID index, never the per-position API.
data_sources: ZTF DR24 light-curve + objects HATS on S3 (s3://ipac-irsa-ztf/ztf/enhanced/dr24/{lc,objects}/hats, anonymous; nested hmjd/mag/magerr/catflags)
IRSA TAP ztf.ztf_current_meta_sci (61.3M quadrant-image rows: obsjd, field/ccdid/qid polygon corners, maglimit, seeing, infobits, programid) pulled per field (1,185 fields)
IRSA TAP ztf.ztf_current_meta_ref (196,357 reference products; 165,870 = 84.5% pre-2019 with maglimit>=21.0) for reference epoch and depth
Gaia DR3 HATS (PM, neighbours within 4", CMD tier M_G<2.5) and GALEX NUV for the blue tier
LS DR10 forced unWISE W1-W4 (W1>19.3 Vega) as dust/RCB prior and AGN veto (W1-W2>0.8); PS1/LS/DECam faint-state detections where available
ALeRCE public API (isdiffpos-negative alerts in gaps, zero positive alerts); Lasair-ZTF objects table (ncand, ncandgp, ncandgp_14, srmag1) with the user's existing token
Novelty gate: VSX/AAVSO, SIMBAD, Gaia DR3 vari, Chen+2020, Tzanidakis+2025 81 dippers, van Roestel+2026 WD list, TNS; Duffy+2024 VY Scl sample and PolarCat as positive controls
credit_channel: VSX new-variable submissions (RCB:, VY:/NL, AM, E with long total eclipse, UXOR:) with the gap, control star, per-frame limits and any archival faint-state detection shown, following the 2026-09-18 VSX lessons; same-day filing for the Lasair twin; AstroNote for RCB/occultation-class or ongoing low states; community-confirm: Kenworthy group (long eclipses), Tisserand/Karambelkar (RCB spectra), Tzanidakis/Davenport (occultations), AAVSO campaigns for V<15.
why_not_already_done: ZTF DR publishes detections only, so every published dip search scores rows inside the dip: Tzanidakis & Davenport 2025 (63M FGK dwarfs, >=50 detections per filter), ASAS-SN big dippers (V<17), SNAD DR23 anomaly features; Duffy+2024 explicitly could not measure the depth of lows that fell in gaps; brokers drop negative-flux alerts. van Roestel+2026 (arXiv:2609.08923) ran negative alerts but only on 273k Gaia white dwarfs (4,027 visually inspected, 6 new 25-100% obscurations) and extending alerts to 1e8 field stars is junk-dominated. ngoodobs was never framed as a completeness statistic; anyone trying it naively sees a 97%-edge-jitter tail and abandons it, because the per-frame polygons and limits live in a separate metadata table nobody joins to the objects table. Not a recycle of the closed bimodal state-cycler lane: that search required both states detected (its <0.01 deg^-2 limit was measured with the >=3-mag tail excluded by censoring); this lane targets systems whose low state produces no rows at all.

title: Gaia DR4 day-1 single-eclipse / single-dip search via TAP-only vari_summary statistics, aimed at the 2014-2020 southern faint window (G 14-19, dec<-30) no other survey covered
merged_from: R5: Gaia DR4 day-1 single-eclipse / single-dip search via TAP-only vari_summary statistics
summary: Stars with one deep, unrepeated dimming in Gaia's 66-month epoch photometry (25 Jul 2014 - 20 Jan 2020): single-eclipse long-period binaries (epsilon Aur / EE Cep / J1407-type disk eclipsers, wide dark-companion eclipses), big-dipper dust/disk occultations, VVV-WIT-08-class giant blinks. Unique window: G 14-19 at dec<-30 (no ZTF; ATLAS-south from 2022; ASAS-SN V to ~17) plus all-sky G>17 before 2018. DR3 released epoch photometry for only 10.5M pre-selected variables; DR4 (2 Dec 2026) gives all 2.8G sources plus a 403,061,676-row vari_summary, and there is no single-dip module among the DR4 variability tables (eclipsing_binary 2.39M is period-based; microlensing 1,360; short_timescale 8.4M; LPV 4.4M). Stage 1 (TAP only, weeks 1-2): num_selected_g_fov>=30, median-min>=0.4 mag, max-median<=0.10 mag, skewness>=+1.5, dip depth >=8x robust scatter; ~1e5-3e5 survivors. Stage 2: DataLink epoch_photometry in 5,000-ID chunks; require >=2 FOV transits inside the dip (paired transits ~106 min apart, the rule-10 analogue), unflagged transits, consistent BP/RP drop. Stage 3: remove periodic/catalogued sources; external repeat checks (ZTF/ATLAS/ASAS-SN/NSC meas/VVV). Censoring channel: a dip >2.7 mag on a G~18 star falls below the G~20.7 onboard limit and appears as missing transits, so compare actual transit epochs to GOST-predicted visits. Expected ~300-500 detectable single-dip systems all-sky (ASAS-SN rate ~5e-7 per star-year scaled to 403M sources over 5.5 yr with 25-40% double-catch probability), ~100-200 in the unique window and new-to-knowledge. Preparation Oct-Nov 2026 on DR3 (same vari_summary columns): recover TYC 2505-672-1, EE Cep-type objects and the ASAS-SN 31 big dippers that have DR3 epoch photometry. Time-boxed Dec 2026 - Feb 2027; expect archive congestion in week 1.
data_sources: Gaia DR4 (2 Dec 2026): gaiadr4.vari_summary (403,061,676 rows), vari_classifier_result (315M), vari_eclipsing_binary (2.39M), DataLink epoch_photometry and epoch_astrometry for survivors
Gaia DR3 vari_summary + epoch_photometry (10.5M sources) for pipeline development and template recovery before 2 Dec
ASAS-SN big-dipper sample (JoHantgen, Rowan, Kochanek+2025: 31 objects at 13<g<14) and TYC 2505-672-1 as recovery controls
ZTF DR24/25, ATLAS, ASAS-SN Sky Patrol, NSC DR2 nsc_dr2.meas, VVV for post-2018 or southern repeat checks; Gaia Observation Forecast Tool (GOST) for predicted-vs-actual transit counts
SIMBAD/VSX/Gaia DR3 classification tables to remove catalogued periodic variables
credit_channel: VSX new-variable submissions with Gaia DR4 epoch photometry as evidence (EA with period unknown; DIP for dust/disk dippers), named credit per object; AstroNote for any class-level result (Gaia-only disk-eclipser candidate); co-authored paper if a professional group takes follow-up. Filing within the first 2-4 weeks is the whole game; VSX form logic and drafts prepared before 2 Dec.
why_not_already_done: It cannot be done before 2 Dec 2026. DPAC CU7 (Eyer, Rimoldini, Holl) classify periodic classes; a one-off dip is not a class their supervised pipeline emits and no dip table is in the DR4 contents list. Kochanek/Rowan/JoHantgen (ASAS-SN) will extend at the bright end, Tzanidakis/Davenport in ZTF, El-Badry-type groups will spend the first months on NSS/astrometric binaries. Their constraint is priority, not capability; the amateur's edge is a pipeline validated on DR3 in advance, a TAP-only pre-filter avoiding the 7.2 TB epoch_photometry download, and willingness to hand-vet a few hundred candidates and file to VSX within weeks. Window ~1-3 months.

title: SPHEREx Galactic-plane point-source engine: (A) first Paschen-alpha / Brackett-alpha emission-line census of obscured stars behind A_V 8-25; (B) weekly 'new mid-IR source since NEOWISE died' sweep of the southern plane
merged_from: R4: First all-sky Paschen-alpha / Brackett-alpha point-source census: obscured emission-line stars (symbiotics, Be/B[e], Wolf-Rayet, PNe) behind A_V 8-25 in the Galactic plane
R3: SPHEREx-native 'new mid-IR source since NEOWISE died' sweep of the southern Galactic plane (obscured novae, eruptive YSOs, dusty mergers)
summary: One forced-PSF-photometry engine on SPHEREx QR2 spectral-image MEFs (anonymous S3, weekly since Oct 2025, two all-sky passes done Dec 2025 and ~May 2026, no point-source catalog yet) feeds two products. (A) Emission-line census: Pa-alpha 1.875 um sits in the telluric water band and has never been surveyed from the ground; IPHAS/VPHAS+ H-alpha reach only A_V<~6-8. Targets: VVV/VVVX + UKIDSS GPS + 2MASS point sources K<=14.0, isolated (no neighbour within 12" brighter than K+1), |b|<=3, l=10-350 (exclude |l|<10), ~2,000 deg^2, ~1e7 targets. Line index E=(F_line-F_cont)/F_cont with continuum from flanking channels; channel width at Pa-alpha ~457 A so E>=0.15 = EW>=~70 A (Br-alpha at R~130: ~310 A, EW>=~47 A); require |E|>=0.15 at >=5 sigma, continuum SNR>=20, in BOTH passes and in >=2 lines (Pa-alpha+Br-alpha, Pa-alpha+Pa-beta, or He I 1.083+Br-gamma). Tier A (WR/symbiotic/PN-like, E>=0.5 in >=3 lines): ~100-500 objects; Tier B (Be-like, E 0.15-0.5): ~2,000-5,000, about half uncatalogued. Missing populations: symbiotics ~300 confirmed vs 3e3-4e5 predicted; Galactic WR ~700 known vs 1,900+/-250 predicted (missing ~1,000 at A_K 1-3, K 10-14); obscured Be/B[e] ~1e4 at K<14 vs a few thousand catalogued. Controls: >=80% of BeSS Be stars K<12 with known Pa-alpha emission, >=95% of catalogued WR K<13; IPHAS/VPHAS+ emitter lists as external truth at A_V<6. FP channels: variability across the ~2-week per-pass exposure spread, the 1.8-2.0 um H2O trough of M giants (demand Pa-beta or Br-alpha confirmation), CO bandhead, crowding, LVF edge rows. (B) New-source sweep: |b|<=5, l=280 through 0 to +30, dec<-20 prioritised (~1,100 deg^2): source at >=5 sigma in >=3 channels of bands 4-6 from exposures at different times and detector positions, W1-eq<=15.0 / W2-eq<=13.5 Vega, with no unWISE NEO7/CatWISE counterpart within 6" brighter than W1=17, no NEOWISE 2014-2024 single-exposure detection, no 2MASS/VVV K<=14 at the PM-propagated position. Single-pass 5-sigma depth ~17.1-18.1 AB at 3.8-5.0 um (the published 17.8-18.8 AB is 4-pass cumulative). Nova rate 47.9 (+3.1/-8.3)/yr (De+2023) vs ~10-15/yr optical; NEOWISE recovered ~22 missed novae in 10 yr, so expect ~3-6 missed novae plus ~10-30 eruptive YSOs/dusty transients over the 16 months of QR2 (May 2025 - Sep 2026), most south of dec -20 where no IR time-domain survey operates (WINTER/PGIR north; VVVX ended 2023; Gattini ended). ~1e3 raw candidates per 1,000 deg^2 per pass, dominated by H2RG persistence latents (fixed in detector coordinates) and 6.2"-pixel blends resolved in VVV/UKIDSS; MPChecker for asteroids near l~0-10. Control: recover the 3 novae and 2 FUors of Karambelkar, De et al. 2026 ApJL blind. Volume: ~4,600 MEFs (~180 GB) per pass for (B); ~17,000 MEFs (~0.7 TB) per pass for (A), streamed and discarded on enzo. Run (B) weekly on the freshest images and file same day.
data_sources: SPHEREx QR2 spectral-image MEFs, all six detectors (bands 4-6 for the sweep), s3://nasa-irsa-spherex anonymous; IRSA SIA2 collection spherex_qr2 (~1-day ingestion lag) for per-position channel completeness
Target list: VVV/VVVX + UKIDSS GPS + 2MASS point sources K<=14.0 Vega with isolation cut; VVV/UKIDSS at 0.34-0.9" for blend control
unWISE full-depth NEO7 coadds, CatWISE2020, NEOWISE single-exposure photometry 2014-Aug 2024, LS DR10 forced unWISE (W1>19.3 Vega) as the static mid-IR reference
Gaia DR3 (astrometry, XP colours, RUWE; propagate every source within 15" to 2025.5), 2MASS J-K, Gaia DR3 LPV table

Templates/controls: BeSS Be catalogue, Rosslowe & Crowther WR catalogue (~700), NODSV symbiotic database (~300), HASH PNe, IPHAS Witham+2008 (4,853 emitters), VPHAS+ emitters; Karambelkar+2026 novae/FUors
ZTF DR24/25, ATLAS forced photometry for optical absence; MPC/MPChecker; TNS cone search; Gaia DR4 epoch photometry (2 Dec 2026) for variability evidence on emission-line finds
credit_channel: (B): TNS AT report + AstroNote with the SPHEREx spectrum (discovery credit = first filer; 'first SPHEREx-discovered nova' is an honest object-specific claim), VSX once classified; IR spectroscopy by De/Karambelkar/Sokoloski or Munari/Woodward as co-authored confirmation. (A): VSX per object once variability is shown (BE/GCAS, ZAND, WR; Gaia DR4 epoch photometry supplies it at scale), plus a catalogue paper (A&A/RNAAS) with Crowther/Rosslowe (WR), Merc/Munari/Akras (symbiotics), Drew/Mohr-Smith (OB/Be) taking the confirming spectra.
why_not_already_done: No point-source catalog or transient pipeline exists for SPHEREx (planned within three years; arXiv:2607.02809 'transient flagging' is about particle hits); the LVF design and 3-6" PSF make classical difference imaging awkward, so nobody has built subtraction or plane forced photometry. The SPHEREx Galactic working group publishes diffuse maps (Murgia+2026 Br-alpha/PAH) and ultracool-dwarf spectra. Karambelkar/De/Hillenbrand/Sokoloski used NEOWISE 2014-2024 ZOGY as their discovery engine and SPHEREx only for classification; their stated future is WINTER/PGIR/PRIME/Cryoscope, northern or not flying, and they do not file TNS reports for plane events. Emission-line specialists (Drew, Crowther, Merc, BeSS) are optical/spectroscopic and small; Crowther's group just spent its effort on Gaia XP WR candidates. What changed vs the dead IR-nova lane: that lane mined NEOWISE/VVV archives De's group had exhausted; this uses a new 2025-26 epoch on a mission with no transient product. Window 6-18 months until a team catalog or De-group SPHEREx differencing appears.

title: Deep/total eclipsing white-dwarf binaries beyond every published search: north via phase-coherent censored misses in ZTF DR24 (Gaia WD locus, G 18.5-20.8), south via DES back-to-back filter-pair drops at r 20-21.5 (dec<-30)
merged_from: R0: Censored-eclipse hunt: total and deep eclipsers hidden in ZTF's detection-only light curves (Gaia white-dwarf locus + bridge, G 18.5-20.8)
R19: Southern deep-eclipse census from DES wide-survey back-to-back filter pairs: point sources at r = 20-21.5 that vanish by >= 1.2 mag in two exposures taken 2.0 min apart
summary: Detached WD+dM, WD+BD and double-WD eclipsers whose eclipses exceed the per-frame headroom (depth >~1.5-3 mag), which leave no in-eclipse rows in ZTF and were found by prior searches only when a partial-eclipse point survived. North (R0): ~140k Gaia EDR3 WD candidates (P_WD>0.75; 1,280,266 candidates / ~359k P_WD>0.75 total) at dec>-28, G 18.5-20.8 plus ~50k bridge objects (M_G 6-11, BP-RP<0.6, parallax_over_error>3); ~200k targets with >=300 good ZTF frames each. Per frame compute an empirical detection probability p_i calibrated on the 200 nearest reference sources within +/-0.2 mag in the same quadrant-epoch; flag 'impossible misses' (p_i>0.98, no row); candidate = >=6 impossible misses AND miss fraction >=3x the matched control; then binary BLS (detected=1/miss=0) over 0.04-2 d with a phased-miss coherence statistic at >4 sigma vs shuffled epochs. Funnel 200k -> 2-4k -> ~300 -> ZFPS forced photometry on <=200 -> 30-80 confirmed. Expected population 300-1,000 eclipsers in the bin (close-binary fraction 3-5%, eclipse probability 8-15%) vs ~150-250 known eclipsing WD+MS in all catalogues combined, mostly G<19 (Parsons 2015 ~71; van Roestel 2021 18; Kosakowski 2022 4; Brown 2023 43; Rebassa-Mansergas 2025 63/920). FP: fixed-(field,ccdid,qid) miss geometry (require misses across >=2 quadrants), PM drift (Gaia PM x 8 yr >1" kills), seeing-correlated blends. HARD GATE added from this batch: van Roestel+2026 (arXiv:2609.08923) ran negative alerts on 273k Gaia WDs, the same parent; before any labour, show from their selection rules that minute-scale periodic dropouts were excluded (they targeted weeks-to-years obscurations); if not, the northern branch is scooped and only the southern branch runs. South (R19): NSC DR2 DES wide footprint (5,000 deg^2, dec -30 to -65 plus Stripe 82), quiescent r 20-21.5; DES visits are back-to-back filter pairs 2.0 min apart (verified from nsc_dr2.exposure), mean ndet 47, ndetr 9.7; candidate = point source vanishing by >=1.2 mag in both exposures of a pair with flags=0, fwhm and centroid consistent. Expected 50-150 WD-dominated eclipsers in the footprint (WD density 10-25 deg^-2 at r 20-21.5, PCEB fraction 2-3%, eclipsing ~10%, depth >1.2 mag in ~40%), P(>=1 in-eclipse exposure) 60-85%, both pair members in eclipse 50-70% => 20-90 pair-corroborated candidates plus 0-3 double-WD/WD+BD and hundreds of deep Algols. Controls: known total/deep eclipsers at G>19 (van Roestel 2021, Kosakowski 2022) north; Parsons+2015 / Gaia-WDMS-2025 eclipsers with DES coverage south. Same pipeline re-runs on nsc_dr2.meas in the DES-SN deep fields for r 21-24 halo WD eclipsers (~3-10 expected in 27 deg^2). Labour ~2-3 weeks north, ~2 weeks south.
data_sources: ZTF DR24 light-curve + objects HATS on S3 (bulk, no per-position limit); IRSA TAP ztf.ztf_current_meta_sci (obsjd, quadrant corners, maglimit, seeing)
Gaia EDR3 white-dwarf catalogue (Gentile Fusillo+2021) and Gaia DR3 astrometry (PM, RUWE, parallax_over_error)
ZTF forced-photometry service (ZFPS, TU Delft account, batches <=1,500) for <=200 finalists
nsc_dr2.object (per-band rms, ndet, ndetr, class_star, pmra/pmdec), nsc_dr2.meas (mag_auto and mag_aper2, flags, fwhm, per-row ra/dec), nsc_dr2.exposure (pair timing) via anonymous Data Lab TAP
Legacy Surveys DR10 (neighbours/blends, forced unWISE W1), DES DR2/DELVE colours, VHS J/Ks for the companion SED

Prior-art / controls: van Roestel+2021 (arXiv:2105.14028), Kosakowski+2022, Brown+2023 (arXiv:2302.11392), Rebassa-Mansergas+2025 (arXiv:2505.15895), Burdge+2020, arXiv:2608.19493, van Roestel+2026 (arXiv:2609.08923), Parsons+2015, VSX
credit_channel: VSX EA (WD+dM) with period plus ZTF DR + ZFPS in-eclipse forced-flux evidence north; VSX EA/EA: with two in-eclipse pair points and composite-SED argument south; low-state by-catch as VSX subtype revision / AAVSO alert. Community-confirm: Warwick/Sheffield (Parsons), Barcelona/UPC (Rebassa-Mansergas), van Roestel, SAAO/ULTRACAM-NTT users for periods and RVs; amateur eclipse timers for G<19.
why_not_already_done: van Roestel/Burdge, Rebassa-Mansergas/Parsons and Brown et al. searched ZTF DR3-DR10 detections with BLS and faint-outlier statistics; total eclipses below the 5-sigma frame limit produce no rows (their own papers note in-eclipse fluxes 'at or below the ZTF detection threshold' for BD companions). ZFPS at 1e5 positions is impractical and Rubin will deliver forced photometry natively, so the rational group move is to wait (DP1 data-rights-only, public stream dark). A missing-epoch statistic joined to the exposure table is engineering, not a paper topic, and DR24 doubles their baseline. South: the 2025 Gaia DR3 WDMS catalogue states only 920 of 1,312 systems are accessible to ZTF and finds its 67 eclipsers only with ZTF/CRTS; Kilic's DECam minute-cadence survey found 1 eclipsing WD+dM in one 3 deg^2 pointing (1/1,700 of the area); DES stellar-variability work modelled RR Lyrae, never pair-drops. Distinct from the running short-duty-cycle EB lane (detection-based) and from the dead Gaia dark-companion lanes (this is a periodic absence in a censored archive, the lever proved on ZTF19abxfaon).

title: Faint southern dwarf-nova / period-bouncer outburst census in DECam per-exposure photometry: DES-SN5YR DiffImg + HELM as the cheap funnel, NSC DR2 meas DES-wide (dec<-31) as the extension, with a hostless halo branch and a censored state-change ledger as by-product
merged_from: R18: Faint recurrent eruptors in the DES-SN/HELM legacy fields: mine the public DES-SN5YR DiffImg candidate list for stellar-coincident outbursters, confirm recurrence with HELM DR1 and NSC per-exposure quiescence
R1: Halo dwarf novae frozen in the DES-SN 2013-2018 seasons: hostless blue outbursts at r_peak 19-23 with no quiescent counterpart to r~26
N5: Lane 2 (structural fix of the closed turn-on lane): same-instrument outburst census in NSC DR2 per-exposure DECam photometry, quiescent r=21.5-24.5 in the DES south (dec<-31)

R20: Deep-vs-deep state-change ledger in the DES-SN + HELM fields: sources at r = 20-22.5 that switch state for >= 10 days or permanently across 2013-2022 (kept only as a by-product of the same data pulls)
summary: Same-instrument (DECam vs DECam) outburst census where no r>20 time-domain survey existed in 2013-2019. Stage 1, cheapest (R18, ~1 week): the public DES-SN5YR release (31,636 DiffImg candidate light curves, griz, 5 seasons, 7-day cadence over 27 deg^2 in 10 fields) cross-matched to static point sources at r_q 21-24.5 in the DES Y3 deep coadds (r~26-27), with recurrence confirmed in HELM DR1 (2019A-2022A, 3-6 d cadence) and quiescence dated in nsc_dr2.meas (field C3 alone has 844 r / 1,182 g / 1,088 i / 1,892 z exposures 2012-2019, 10-sigma r~21.8); CV column density at |b|=45-65 is 0.2-0.6 deg^-2 so 5-16 CVs in 27 deg^2, ~70% with r_q>21 => 3-7 new faint DN (candidate period bouncers) plus <0.5 expected exotic bycatch (qLMXB/UCXB in CDF-S/XMM-LSS, AM CVn). Stage 2, halo branch (R1): hostless blue outbursts r_peak 19-23, g-r<0.3, 1-4 week duration, no DES deep-coadd counterpart within 1" (r~26.5 in C3/X3/E2, ~25.5 elsewhere), no LS DR10 galaxy within 3" to r 24.5, >=3 meas detections on >=2 nights within 40 d (rule 10), centroid scatter <0.3" and no linear motion; expected 3-12 halo outbursts (5e4 halo CVs, ~25 in the 27 deg^2 cone to 50 kpc, recurrence 5-30 yr) plus 5-20 thick-disc SU UMa outbursts at r_peak 16.5-19.5 in E1/E2 (dec -43). Stage 3, extension (N5, 1-2 weeks): NSC DR2 DES-wide footprint (~5,000 deg^2, |b|>20, dec<-31): object pre-cut ndet>=6, median r 21.5-24.5, class_star>0.7; outburst = >=2 same-night measurements (DES takes griz of a hex within ~10 min) or >=2 nights, each >=2.0 mag above the object median and >=0.5 mag above depth10sig, fwhm within 30% of exposure fwhm, asemi/bsemi<1.3, flags=0, centroid within 0.5"; hostless branch = >=2 same-night measurements within 0.7" with no NSC object and no LS DR10 source r<24.5 within 1". Depth arithmetic (Pala+2020 4.8e-6 pc^-3, scale height ~280 pc): 0.10-0.15 CVs deg^-2 to r=23.5 at |b|>30 => 500-750 CVs in the footprint, essentially none catalogued (VSX/Gaia CV lists complete to r~19-20); ~30 epochs per position, duty cycle 2-5% => 0.4-0.7 chance per CV of >=1 caught outburst => 200-400 outbursters in the data, 100-300 recoverable, 10-20 of them hostless period-bouncer candidates (quiescent M_r~12-13, r>24.5 at 2-3 kpc). Vetoes: LS type != PSF, W1-W2>0.8, quiescent r-z>1.2 (M-dwarf flares), |beta|<10 deg for single-night hostless events, DES-SN5YR/TNS match within 2". nsc_dr2.object variable10sig is MAD-based and must not be used as a positive selector. By-product (R20): with the same chip-footprint ledger (nsc_dr2.chip, ~50k CCD footprints for the 10 pointings; 2,008 point sources deg^-2 at r 20-22.5; ~54,000 objects x ~2,500 covering exposures) record >=10-day or permanent state switches as censored faint-state measurements, expected only 1-4 state-switching magnetic CVs and 0-2 oddities. Controls: recover VSX UG-type CVs with dec<-31 and DES coverage (a few dozen) and CRTS/ASAS-SN dwarf novae inside S1/S2/X fields; inject 2, 3, 4 mag outbursts; stop rule: <70% of known outbursts recovered with >=2 same-night measurements closes the lane. Data Lab TAP anonymous (rejects q3c and ADQL POINT/CIRCLE; use ra/dec boxes); meas pulls object-driven in async batches.
data_sources: DES-SN5YR public release (31,636 DiffImg candidate light curves; GitHub/Zenodo, no account) and Pursiainen+2018 RET list for exclusion
HELM DR1 (Zhang+2024 ApJS 274, 42; 2019A-2022A) per-field light curves via open HTTP directory

nsc_dr2.exposure (mjd, filter, exptime, fwhm, depth10sig, depth95), nsc_dr2.meas (67.8e9 rows: per-exposure mag_auto/mag_aper2, ra/dec, fwhm, asemi/bsemi, class_star, flags), nsc_dr2.object, nsc_dr2.chip via anonymous Data Lab TAP

DES DR2 coadd and DES Y3 deep-field catalogue (Hartley+2022, r~26-27 in C3/X3/E2/COSMOS) for quiescent-counterpart limits; LS DR10 (Tractor type, griz, forced unWISE W1-W4) for AGN/galaxy veto and quiescent colours
CRTS, ASAS-SN, ATLAS, ZTF ZFPS (dec>-31 sliver only), SkyMapper DR4 per-epoch photometry (anonymous TAP, r~21) for recurrence and bright-end control; VSX/SIMBAD/TNS/Gaia CV lists as novelty gate
VHS J/Ks and Gaia DR3 PM for companion/blend checks
credit_channel: VSX (UG/UGSU/UGWZ: with the DECam per-exposure outburst light curve and quiescent photometry; VSX accepts survey-only discoveries); TNS archival AT reports for hostless outbursts (TNS accepts past discovery dates); halo (>10 kpc) or >=5-object population results as a short co-authored note with the CV space-density community (Pala, Inight, Schreiber; DESI 1,029-CV paper arXiv:2607.22836 and eROSITA period-bouncer paper arXiv:2509.17216 show the appetite); Rubin DDF teams (ECDFS/EDFS/ELAIS-S1/XMM-LSS overlap) as follow-up consumers.
why_not_already_done: Everyone who held these photons treated dwarf novae as contamination: DES-SN's DiffImg/AUTOSCAN (Kessler+2015, ~30,000 candidates) and the DES-SN5YR release are SN-selected with a multi-season cut that removed long-lived Galactic objects (the release paper states 75% of DiffImg candidates are not SNe); Pursiainen+2018 required SN-like fits and hosted events; HELM (Shen/Zhang) is an AGN reverberation programme and notes it misses sources without a static counterpart; the DECam DDF (Graham+2023/2024) classified stellar variables generically and never published a CV sample; NSC DR2 flags 23M variables with MAD indices a single 2-mag epoch barely moves. Szkody's ZTF CV series is r<20.5 and dec>-31; ATLAS-south started 2022 at o<19.5; CV groups have no DECam deep-field pipeline. The 2013-2019 southern epochs are frozen and cannot be scooped by Rubin; period bouncers should be 40-70% of CVs by theory but are a few per cent observed. Structural fix of the closed turn-on lane: DECam is compared to DECam (same PSF, pipeline, depth), so blends, sub-threshold noise and cosmic rays cannot satisfy the selection; same-night two-measurement and per-measurement morphology kill the artefact channel.

title: Reference-poisoned outbursters: ZTF sources whose reference co-add window was itself in outburst, so later returns to that state never alert (join DR24 light curves to ztf_current_meta_ref)
merged_from: N3: Reference-poisoned outbursters: sources whose ZTF reference window was itself in outburst (later outbursts never alert)
summary: Objects whose ZTF reference (>=15 frames; window per quadrant from startobsdate/endobsdate in ztf_current_meta_ref, 177,984 rows) was built while they were in a high state, so subsequent returns produce difference flux ~0 and only negative alerts while fading: alert-based CV/transient discovery is structurally blind to them for the lifetime of the reference. Tier 1 (windows <=30 d): dwarf-nova superoutbursts and long normal outbursts, AM CVn outbursts, EXor bursts. Tier 2 (windows of months-years, common for i-band and secondary-grid references): Z Cam standstills, symbiotic and nova-like high states, slow novae, AGN flares, TDEs and SNe. Also Jan-May 2018 transients caught in early references before public alerts (June 2018): ~300 SNe at r<20.5 expected in reference windows, of which tens at 19.5<r<20.5 plausibly never reported. Selection: (1) measure and state the reference-window length distribution first; (2) DR24 objects with >=3 catflags-clean detections inside their own quadrant's window and >=20 outside: in-window median >=1.0 mag brighter than out-window median and >=80% of in-window epochs >=0.7 mag brighter; (3) reject LPV/periodic: Lomb-Scargle 60-1,000 d amplitude >0.8 mag, or in-window mean not a >=5 MAD outlier among rolling 30-day means; (4) recurrence bonus: later returns to within 0.3 mag of the in-window level; (5) centroid consistency in- vs out-window; (6) ALeRCE: zero positive alerts 2018-2025, negative alerts during fades; (7) novelty gates; TNS cone+date for 2018-window transients with host offset; (8) template test: recover the reference-contaminated SNe Ia of Dhawan+2022 (ZTF SN Ia DR1) on the pipeline's own configuration before quoting yield. Budget: ~1e5 raw flags (LPVs dominate the plane), 5,000-10,000 after cuts, 30-50% uncatalogued => 100-300 vetted uncatalogued outbursting systems with zero positive alerts on record. Cheapest lane in the set: one TAP download plus a streaming scan of DR24 HATS partitions on enzo (pyarrow if lsdb absent); pilot 100 fields in a week, full run 2-3 weeks; DR24 parquet lacks refmag/limitmag so selection uses time windows. ALeRCE cone queries only at the ~5,000-object stage, batched, checked for empty-200s. Report the window length with every candidate.
data_sources: IRSA TAP ztf.ztf_current_meta_ref (177,984 rows: field, ccdid, qid, filtercode, nframes, startobsdate, endobsdate, maglimit) -- one download
ZTF DR24 light-curve HATS on S3, joined on fieldid, rcid = 4*(ccdid-1)+(qid-1), filterid
ALeRCE public API (per-object alert list with isdiffpos)
VSX, SIMBAD, TNS, Gaia DR3 vari, GSA, Chen+2020, Healy+2024 (ZTF Source Classification) as novelty gates
ZTF SN Ia DR1 (Dhawan+2022) reference-contaminated SNe as positive controls
Gaia DR3 HATS (isolation/PM) and PS1 OTMO (quiescent state)
credit_channel: VSX new-variable submissions (UG/UGSU/UGZ/ZAND/NL with DR light curves showing the outbursts); TNS archival discovery reports for unreported 2018 transients (discovery date = 2018 epoch); AstroNote for recurrent blind systems of interest (standstills, nova-likes); community-confirm via vsnet/AAVSO/CBA and the ZTF CV group for spectra. The population-level fact (how many ZTF references are poisoned) is a refereeable byproduct.
why_not_already_done: Brokers and alert-based surveys cannot (Szkody+2020 year-1 CVs and the 2023 ML CV-discovery paper both work from alerts). The ZTF SN Ia DR1 paper documented reference contamination but fixed it only for its own SNe; IPAC kept building references through the survey without screening for transients. DR-based catalogues (Chen+2020, Healy+2024, SNAD DR23) never use the reference window as a selection axis because the DR parquet does not carry it; the join to ztf_current_meta_ref costs one TAP query and is the missing step. Generalises the J075308 lesson (442 detections, zero ALeRCE alerts) to a population.

title: Post-Gaia northern microlensing: ZTF DR24 window 2023.2-2025.8 plus the long-tE (>=250 d) and censored-faint-baseline tails, filed to VSX as type 'Microlens'
merged_from: N7: Post-Gaia northern microlensing: ZTF DR24 window 2023.2-2025.8 plus the long-tE and censored-faint-baseline tails, filed to VSX as type 'Microlens'
summary: ~60-90 new microlensing events in the ZTF northern-plane fields (dec>-28, the ~196 rr fields of Zhai+2024 plus g) peaking between 2023-03-09 (end of the DR17 search) and 2025-10-22 (DR24 public cutoff; plane partnership through 2024-07-22), none in any DR-based catalogue; ~30-40 peak after 2025-01-15 when Gaia stopped observing, so they carry no Gaia alert name and are registered nowhere. Two tails no DR search has admitted: (i) tE>=250 d events over the full 7.6-yr baseline (expect 2-6; Zhai's longest was 421 d), the black-hole/neutron-star lens candidates; (ii) faint-baseline events (baseline r 20.5-21.5, peak <=20) that fail Zhai's >=30-point rule by detection censoring, expected ~40-80 over the DR span, many sitting unfiled in the alert stream. Selection: fields dec>-28, |b|<=20; single brightening episode over the whole DR, amplitude >=0.5 mag (bright) or >=1.0 mag above the censored baseline (faint); t0 in [2023-03-09, 2025-10-22]; >=6 detections in the peak window; rise/fall ratio 0.7-1.4; achromatic |delta(g-r)|<0.1; PSPL chi2_red<3 preferred over sinusoid/flare/DN templates; baseline r 14-21.5; per-epoch centroid scatter <0.3" vs PS1/Gaia; mag-vs-limitmag slope ~0. All-sky for the tE>=250 d tail with amplitude >=0.3 mag and >=24 months of pre/post baseline. Funnel: Fink microlensing-tagged objects first (few 1e3, Ban+2025 module), then a streaming 'max-minus-median >=0.5 mag and single-episode' scan of HATS plane partitions. FPs: DN/CV outbursts (fast rise, bluer, recurrent), YSO/Be (red, W1-W2 excess), LPV maxima, AGN flares (extended host), blends/threshold artefacts, and OGLE-IV EWS events in bulge-adjacent fields (l~0-30, dec -28 to -20): cone-check EWS lists. Control: recover Zhai's 124 DR17 events with the DR24 pipeline. Funnel build ~1-2 weeks, ~2-4 h vetting per filed event; events peaking after 2025-10-22 are alert-only until DR25; sweep the freshest window first and file same-day.
data_sources: ZTF DR24 bulk light curves via IRSA HATS/parquet (public through MJD 60970 = 2025-10-22)
ZTF DR24 exposure table: per-frame limitmag and per-epoch centroids
Fink broker API microlensing-tagged objects 2023-2026 (Ban+2025) as the funnel; ALeRCE API for alert cross-check and stamp classes
Gaia DR3 (parallax/PM/colour; source distance for tE), Pan-STARRS DR2 + LS DR10 (baseline mags, morphology), LS DR10 forced unWISE W1/W2
OGLE-IV EWS 2023-2026 event lists; VSX + TNS cone searches; GSA archive for pre-2025 Gaia names
Prior art: Rodriguez+2022 (DR5, 60 events), Zhai+2024 (DR17, 124+54 events)
credit_channel: VSX type 'Microlens' (type exists; precedent GSC 03656-01328 = Gaia16aye; user's VSX account live); TNS AT + microlensing classification once TNS registration (task #152) completes (Gaia precedent AT2021uey); long-tE survivors to BHTOM/Wyrzykowski or Lam/Lu for parallax modelling as a co-authored note.
why_not_already_done: DR-based searches lag ~2 yr and impose >=30 points + coverage cuts: Rodriguez+2022 and Zhai+2024 (Caltech) are the only catalogues; Medford/Lam/Lu (PUZLE/zort) had no DR2x sequel by mid-2026. Gaia Science Alerts, the only all-sky microlensing filer to TNS, ended 2025-01-15. Fink's module tags candidates but nobody files them. OGLE-IV EWS covers only 208 bulge fields in 2026. The censored faint-baseline population is excluded by construction from every DR search. Northern events peaking 2025-2026 have zero registry entries.

title: Near-IR archive state changes and events anchored on 2MASS (1997-2001): 2MASS vs UHS/VHS turn-ons/turn-offs, 2MASS-vs-Gaia optical-deficit stars in pre-2012 dust declines, and the PGIR 0.5-2 mag 'excluded middle' on optically-dark stars at |b|>5
merged_from: R15: Lane NIR-1: Pre-WISE-gap turn-ons and turn-offs -- 2MASS (1997-2001) vs the three accidental UHS epochs (J 2012-17 / K 2017-24 / H 2019-24) and VHS, at |b|>5
R17: Lane NIR-3: Optical-off / infrared-on -- 2MASS (2000) vs Gaia DR3 mean-G (2014.5-2017.4) optical-deficit selection for stars in multi-year dust declines and long eclipses
R16: Lane NIR-2: The PGIR 'excluded middle' -- short-lived and 0.5-2 mag J-band events on optically-dark 2MASS stars at |b|>5 (nightly cadence, 2018-2022)
summary: Three branches on one substrate (2MASS PSC + WSA/VSA + Data Lab, all anonymous), each targeting objects that are constant in every survey able to see variability and therefore unclassified. Branch A (R15): objects whose near-IR state changed by >=1.5-2.5 mag between 2MASS (1997.5-2001.1) and ~2012 and then stayed changed (flat in unTimely 2010-2020, VarWISE, Gaia DR3, ZTF, PGIR): decade-long FU Ori-type outbursts erupted 2001-2012 outside Spitzer-covered clouds (~30-40 FUors known), symbiotic slow novae (PU Vul class, ~3 per half-century), dust-thinning OH/IR brightenings (arXiv:2008.06897, only measured in the plane); fading direction: Ks<12.5 in 2000 and >=2.5 mag fainter or absent in ALL three UHS epochs (J 2012-17, K 2017-24, H 2019-24) or VHS -- dust-cocoon events (V605 Aql-type), multi-year total eclipses, a near-IR VASCO analogue never attempted. ~25M-row extractions in dec strips under the WSA 30-min cap; Gaia PM propagation of every match to the 2MASS scan epoch; 15-70 VSX-grade objects for ~2 weeks of mostly image vetting; odds >=1 genuinely new eruptive/vanished object 50-70%, >=1 FUor-class 20-30%. Branch B (R17): stars normal-coloured and optically bright in 1998-2001 whose Gaia DR3 mean G (2014.5-2017.4) is >=2.5 mag (or >=4 mag if Gaia-absent) too faint for their 2MASS J-Ks along the extinction vector -- declines begun before 2012 and unrecovered by 2018, invisible to Tisserand 2020 WISE colours, ASAS-SN (Shields+2019), Karambelkar+2021/2024 ZTF/PGIR declines and the Gaia DR3 classifier (153 RCBs), all of which need the decline inside their own window; ~160 Galactic RCBs known vs several hundred predicted; 5-25 new RCB/DY Per candidates and 1-10 long-eclipse/cocoon systems for ~1 week (one ADQL job, ~1e3-scale vetting); unTimely mid-IR rise anti-correlated with the optical fade, UHS/VHS K persistence, PGIR/ZTF recovery and the SPHEREx 2-5 um hot-dust bump make a self-contained decline-by-dust case; Gaia DR4 epoch photometry (2 Dec 2026) dates every candidate. Branch C (R16): days-to-months 0.5-2 mag J-band events on optically invisible or extremely red 2MASS stars at |b|>5 in PGIR DR1 (dec>-29, 2018-10 to ~2022-10, 1-3 night cadence; 149M-row sources table, 47.6-billion-row photometry at Data Lab): obscured Z And-type symbiotic outbursts (0.5-1.5 mag J rises over 30-300 d; 1e3-1e5 predicted vs ~300 known), embedded-YSO bursts and dips in Taurus/Perseus/Oph/Orion/lambda Ori/Mon R2/Cepheus that NEOWISE cannot resolve in time (6-month cadence) or space (6" pixels), RCB mini-declines whose optical counterpart fell in a ZTF gap, and unexplained IR-only events; the PGIR team's own census (128 stars, 92% at |b|<15) selected only >=2 mag, >50 epochs, smooth persistent variables. First cut is one async SQL, photometry pulls for <=1e4 sources; >=10 new VSX-grade objects ~70%, >=1 obscured symbiotic outburst ~40%, >=1 physically novel IR-only event ~25%; ~1-2 weeks. Vetting stack shared by all branches: UHS/VHS epochs, unTimely W1/W2, ZTF DR (state via gaps), SPHEREx QR2 0.75-5 um spectrophotometry per target (emission lines = symbiotic/nova; dust bump = RCB), Gaia DR4 epochs. IRSA per-position use stays under ~1,100 (shortlists only).
data_sources: 2MASS PSC 1997.5-2001.1 (ph_qual, cc_flg, prox, scan date, XSC exclusion), local copy or Data Lab twomass.psc

UHS DR3 at WSA (uhsSource/uhsDetection/uhsDetectionAll; J 2012-17, K 2017-24, H 2019-24) and VHS DR6 at VSA (per-detection MJD, 2009-2021), with XNeighbour tables to 2MASS; WSA/VSA freeform SQL, no account
PGIR DR1 at NOIRLab Data Lab (sources table 149M rows, photometry 47.6e9 rows; dec>-29, 2018-10 to ~2022-10)
Gaia DR3 gaia_source (phot_g_mean_mag, phot_g_n_obs, PM for propagation to 2MASS epoch; Gaia-absent sources kept as a class) and Gaia DR4 epoch photometry from 2 Dec 2026
unTimely W1/W2 (16 epochs 2010-2020) and VarWISE; ZTF DR24 light curves for the optical state (gaps included); SPHEREx QR2 per-target spectrophotometry

Novelty gates: VSX, SIMBAD, Gaia DR3 vari_classifier and LPV tables, Tisserand 2020 WISE-RCB list, Gaia DR3 RCB class, ASAS-SN RCB lists, Contreras Pena & Lucas UKIDSS extreme variables (618), VVV/VIRAC2 in the bulge strip
credit_channel: VSX (named credit) for every confirmed variable: FUOR/EXOR/YSO, ZAND/symbiotic nova, RCB:/DYPER:, EA with multi-year eclipse, or UNIQUE for vanished/IR-only sources; AstroNote for any object whose SPHEREx 2025-26 spectrum shows the event ongoing; community-confirm: FUor/eruptive-YSO candidates to Contreras Pena / Lucas / Hillenbrand, symbiotics to the SALT symbiotic programme (arXiv:2512.01744) and Munari/Merc, RCB candidates to Tisserand / Clayton / Karambelkar for H-deficiency spectra (these groups solicit candidates and name the finder).
why_not_already_done: The only 2MASS-vs-later-NIR variability comparisons are Contreras Pena & Lucas (UKIDSS GPS, 618 dK>1 stars) and the VVV team, both strictly at |b|<5 because their science is plane YSOs; UHS K and H did not exist until June 2023 / Sept 2025 and the UHS team publishes brown dwarfs, high-PM objects and quasars, not variability; VHS (McMahon, Banerji) used 2MASS-vs-VHS only for quasar ensemble variability (arXiv:2504.16733). Every RCB channel needs the decline or recovery inside its own window (the mirror of the J075308 lesson); Tisserand+2022 used 2MASS+Gaia as a static colour locus, not a 15-year epoch difference. The PGIR census (PASP 2025, arXiv:2510.18959) required peak-to-peak >=2 mag, >50 epochs, von Neumann <=0.2, excluding 0.5-2 mag and short erratic events by construction; PGIR DR1 has been public since Oct 2024 with no external variability census. The NEOWISE variability window is closed (VarWISE + Guidry) but these are different substrates (2MASS/UHS/VHS/PGIR/Gaia) at cadences and resolutions NEOWISE cannot reach.

title: Pre-reference frozen-state census: Gaia DR3 (2014.5-2017.4) sources that are absent from, or >=2.5 mag fainter than predicted in, the ZTF reference catalogue (2018+) with zero positive alerts since -- tight G<=16.5 / >=4.5 mag vanishing core first, staged so Gaia DR4 dates every ingress on 2 Dec 2026
merged_from: N6: Lane 3 (reference-seeding blind spot): Gaia-present / ZTF-absent -- stars at G<=16.5 present in Gaia DR3 that are missing from the 2018 ZTF reference catalogue and have produced no ZTF alert since
R8: Turn-off census: Gaia DR3 sources (2014-2017) that are >=2 mag fainter or absent in the ZTF reference era (2018-2026) - the total-censoring limit, staged for Gaia DR4 epoch photometry

N2: Frozen-state stars: Gaia DR3 (2014-17) vs ZTF reference (2018+) discordance >= 2.5 mag, both directions, with no alert ever issued (fade direction only; the 'appeared' Direction B is dropped separately as R10/N2-B)
summary: State changes that predate the ZTF reference stack generate no difference flux and no DR light-curve object, so both brokers and DR-based searches are blind to them by construction (lessons 2 and 3). Tier 0, run first (N6, ~1 week): Gaia DR3 G<=16.5, phot_g_n_obs>=30, astrometric_params_solved=31, RUWE<2, duplicated_source=false, PM<300 mas/yr (0.6" drift 2016->2018), no other Gaia source within 3" brighter than G+2, not within 30" of a G<8 star, dec>-28; no ZTF DR24 object in g OR r within 2"; covering reference quadrants with startobsdate<2019 and maglimit>=21.0 in both g and r (84.5% of 196,357 products qualify) => a >=4.5 mag fade; no positive ALeRCE/Lasair alert 2018-2026 within 2"; vetoes: VSX/TNS/Gaia-alert nova or SN within 5" dated 2014-2018, Gaia DR3 Mira/LPV class, LS DR10 type != PSF. Expected ~6e7 Gaia stars in the cut, ~3e4 raw non-matches (deblending), ~1e3 after isolation and PM cuts, 100-300 for eyeball vetting, 2-10 genuinely novel objects: R CrB stars in decade-long minima (R CrB itself 2007-2018), >=8-yr giant eclipses (Gaia17bpp 7-yr precedent), VY Scl very long low states, dust-cocooned post-AGB objects, and the single archival test able to catch a Galactic vanished star (N6946-BH1 analogue) at G<=16.5. Tier 1 extension (R8/N2, 2-3 weeks): 15.0<G<18.5 (R8: G<18.5, |b|>10, dec>-28, ~1e8 rows), predict r from G and BP-RP (Riello+2021), Tier-1 miss = no DR24 object within 2"; Tier-2 = reference PSF catalogue source >=2.5 mag fainter than predicted (maglimit read per quadrant, never assumed); reject if the nearest ZTF object within 3" matches the SUM of Gaia fluxes inside 3" (blend); ~1e4-1e5 raw misses -> ~500 after coverage + isolation -> ~100 after the faint-counterpart check -> 10-40 real objects (R8: 5-30), including 2014-2017 slow transients (symbiotic/nova-like outbursts >=1 yr) that entered DR3 as spurious persistent sources, some never reported (5-20). Survivors get IRSA reference cutouts (a few hundred calls), PS1 OTMO 2010-2014 state, unTimely W1/W2 dust trend, and from 2 Dec 2026 the Gaia DR4 epoch light curve of the ingress at zero marginal cost. Controls: 1,000 random Gaia G<=16.5 stars must match a ZTF DR24 object at >=99.9% (stop rule: base mismatch >~1e-3 after isolation means matching is not understood, nothing is filed); known 2014-2017 novae in the footprint must appear as Gaia-present/ZTF-absent before catalogue removal; VSX VY Scl and RCB stars with low states spanning 2018 as positives. FP is bookkeeping, not astrophysics: 2-3" deblending (re-match against the raw reference PSF catalogue, not the DR objects table), reference masks near saturated stars/ghosts/CCD edges (absence required in both bands of every overlapping field), sources in the reference coadd with no single-epoch detection (kept as a separate 'faded during 2018' class), Gaia transients at galaxy outskirts. Run BEFORE 2 Dec 2026 so DR4 epoch photometry is consumed on release day; the R10-style 'appeared' direction costs one extra query on the same crossmatch if wanted.
data_sources: Gaia DR3 gaia_source / HATS at data.lsdb.io (G, BP-RP, PM, RUWE, phot_g_n_obs, duplicated_source, astrometric_params_solved, vari class); count G<17.5 at dec>-31 = 135,907,142 measured
ZTF DR24 objects HATS on S3 (anonymous) for the 2" LSDB cross-match; ZTF reference PSF catalogues (IRSA IBE ref psfcat per field/ccd/quad) for the definitive in-reference test on survivors
IRSA TAP ztf.ztf_current_meta_ref (196,357 products: startobsdate, endobsdate, nframes, maglimit, corner ra/dec) for per-quadrant coverage polygons
ALeRCE and Lasair-ZTF cone searches for any positive alert 2018-2026 within 2"
Pan-STARRS DR2 / PS1 OTMO HATS (2010-2014 state), unTimely W1/W2 (2010-2020) and LS DR10 forced unWISE for dust evolution, LS DR10 morphology, IRSA reference-image cutouts for ~100-300 survivors
Novelty gates: VSX, TNS, Gaia Science Alerts, SIMBAD, Gaia DR3 vari; Gaia DR4 epoch photometry from 2 Dec 2026 for every survivor
credit_channel: VSX new variable (RCB:, VY:/NL, AM, ZAND, EA with multi-year eclipse, or UNIQUE) with Gaia/PS1-bright, ZTF-absent evidence and quantified non-detection limits; TNS archival discovery report for any Gaia-era transient never reported; AstroNote for any >=4-mag, >=8-yr fade of a G<=16.5 star; community-confirm: Kenworthy group (long eclipses), Tisserand/Karambelkar/Crawford+2025 (RCB), VASCO (Villarroel) as co-authoring home for vanished candidates, Gaia alerts team (can pull epoch photometry before DR4).
why_not_already_done: Every ZTF-era fade search works forward from the reference: negative alerts need reference flux (van Roestel+2026), DR light curves need a reference-seeded object (Tzanidakis & Davenport 2025 dropped Gaia stars lacking >=50 detections). Gaia DPAC computes Gaia-ZTF/PS1 crossmatch statistics for completeness but never vets the unmatched tail; the DR3-variable-WD-vs-ZTF comparisons ask whether Gaia variables vary in ZTF, never whether Gaia-bright sources are missing. VASCO (Villarroel+2020, AJ 159, 8; Solano+2022; arXiv:2604.04810) compared USNO-B/POSS-I to PS1 with 70-year baselines and plate defects, stopping at ~100 unresolved candidates; nobody has run the clean 2016-vs-2018 CCD/space version, which is 100x more precise astrometrically and has an 8-yr alert stream to prove non-recovery. It looks like a bookkeeping crossmatch whose raw tail is 99% crowding, and the per-quadrant coverage proof (lesson 9) is the step catalogue-level crossmatchers skip. Gaia DR4 will expose the 2014-2019 fades to everyone in 10 weeks, but 'still faint in 2025' remains a ZTF-only fact. Not a recycle of the closed turn-on lane: fade direction only, with the deep-sharp catalogue (Gaia) as the BRIGHT epoch.

title: Non-thermal Galactic mismatch: parallax/proper-motion veto on gamma-ray, radio and hard-X-ray 'blazar/AGN' catalogues, plus radio-star and WD+M catalogues crossed with sub-day optical periods and Stokes V
merged_from: R12: Parallax veto on non-thermal AGN-candidate catalogues (gamma-ray / radio / hard-X-ray 'blazars' and 'quasars' that are Galactic)
R14: Radio-loud short-period binaries: radio-star catalogues x sub-day optical periods, and WD+M catalogues x Stokes V/I radio
summary: Days of crossmatching for objects whose class membership is wrong in the catalogue that owns them. Branch 1 (R12): Galactic non-thermal emitters filed as blazars/AGN because they sit in AGN colour boxes and were associated with radio, gamma-ray or hard-X-ray sources without an astrometric check: AR Sco-type WD pulsars and magnetic propellers (AR Sco itself has AllWISE W1-W2=0.81, W2-W3=2.57, i.e. the Stern/blazar strip, Gaia parallax 8.54 mas, 5-9 mJy in VLASS/RACS, measured this session), spider MSP binaries inside 4FGL 'bcu' associations, symbiotic X-ray binaries and intermediate polars among the 88%-'extragalactic' eRASS:3 hard-band counterparts. Inputs: 4FGL-DR4 (7,194 sources; 1,625 BCU + ~2,300 bll/fsrq counterparts), WIBRaLS2 (9,541) + KDEBLLACS (5,579), Assef+2018 R90 (4.5M), raw Gaia DR3 qso_candidates (6.6M, ~52% purity), RACS-low2 (3.92M, dec<=+48, 195 uJy rms, Jun 2026), VLASS QL, eROSITA-DE DR2 eRASS:3 main (1,911,744 point sources) + hard 2.3-5 keV; veto = Gaia DR3 parallax or PM at >=5 sigma (or variability/periodicity in ZTF/Gaia) on counterparts within the association radius; largest table 6.6M rows, TOPCAT/astropy on a laptop; ~100-200 vettings at ~10 min each; expected 5-30 uncatalogued Galactic non-thermal objects with a few high-value outcomes (gamma-ray binary, WD pulsar). Only never-cleaned catalogues are inputs: Milliquas v8, Quaia and CatNorth/CatSouth applied Gaia PM cuts but discarded the rejects unpublished. Branch 2 (R14): (A) radio-star catalogues (Sydney Radio Star Catalogue 839, Yiu+2024 VLASS/LoTSS-Gaia, Pritchard RACS-V) entries typed 'M dwarf' or 'unknown' with a UV/XP white-dwarf component and a ZTF/Gaia period <6 h; (B) the Li+2025 Gaia-XP WDMS catalogue (~30,000 within 1 kpc, ~1,700 high-confidence; check for a public copy) on circularly polarised or persistent RACS-low2 / RACS-mid / VLASS E1-E3 / LoTSS DR2 sources -- both exclude what Pelisoli's reverse searches excluded (M-dwarf-dominated PCEBs, exactly the ILT J1101+5521 / GLEAM-X J0704-37 / ASKAP J1745-5051 hosts; theory puts 100-1,000 such systems within 2 kpc); expected 0-3 objects for a few days plus ~50-100 vettings, any confirmed member joining a class with <10 members; (C) the throttled LoTSS/CASDA cutout branch (~30k cutouts, weeks) is deferred unless A/B produce a hit. Novelty gates: SIMBAD, VSX, Gaia DR3 vari classes, Marton+2023 YSOs, HASH PNe, existing gamma-ray binary and spider lists.
data_sources: 4FGL-DR4, WIBRaLS2 + KDEBLLACS, Assef+2018 AllWISE R90, CatWISE2020, Gaia DR3 qso_candidates (VizieR TAP, all confirmed reachable)
RACS-low2 Stokes I/V (CASDA), RACS-mid (VizieR J/other/PASA/41.3), VLASS QL Epochs 1-3 (NRAO/CADC), LoTSS DR2
eROSITA-DE DR2 eRASS:3 main + hard-band catalogues (erodat bulk FITS); 5XMM-DR15 via XCAT-DB/HEASARC for X-ray counterparts
Gaia DR3 astrometry (parallax, PM, RUWE), XP colours; GALEX GUVcat for the WD component
Sydney Radio Star Catalogue (Driessen+2024, 839 stars), Yiu+2024 VLASS/LoTSS-Gaia radio stars, Pritchard RACS-V; Li+2025 Gaia-XP WDMS catalogue
ZTF periodic catalogues (Chen+2020, 781k), Gaia DR3 vari_eclipsing (2.2M), ZTF DR24 light curves for period search on survivors; SIMBAD/VSX/Marton+2023/HASH as novelty gates
credit_channel: VSX for anything with periodic or eruptive optical variability (X-ray/radio/gamma association and 'AR Sco-like' in remarks; named credit, archive-only); TNS AstroNote for a Galactic identification of a 4FGL/eROSITA-hard source or a radio-loud WD-binary identification; community-confirm by Fermi/radio/CV spectroscopists (Strader/Swihart for spiders, Pelisoli/Marsh for WD pulsars, Hurley-Walker and Callingham/de Ruiter for LPT hosts).
why_not_already_done: The Fermi-LAT catalogue team associates via likelihood ratio against radio/WISE lists and never vetoes with Gaia astrometry (4FGL J0647.7-4418 was found to be Galactic by accident); D'Abrusco/Massaro treat the >12% non-blazar-like fraction of WIBRaLS2/KDEBLLACS as contamination, not targets; Flesch, Storey-Fisher and Fu applied PM cuts and threw the rejects away. Radio-first groups (GLEAM-X, V-LoTSS, RACS-V/VAST, CHIME) find pulses then look for counterparts, never starting from WD+M lists; Pelisoli's two reverse searches (846k Gaia WDs x VLASS E1: 0 secure; Gaia-bridge+WISE AR Sco analogues: 56 candidates, 1 new pulsar) exclude M-dwarf-dominated PCEBs; radio-star cataloguers classify by SIMBAD type without testing for a WD component or a sub-day period; the population papers (arXiv:2604.18688, 2509.09224) call for this search but have not run it. New supply since those searches: RACS-low2 (Jun 2026), eROSITA-DE DR2 (31 Jul 2026), 5XMM-DR15 (9 Jun 2026).
